title: Conditional kappa 0.001372554837726243: coordinated gauge collapse with retimed asynchronous whole owners
body:
Conditional kappa = **0.001372554837726243**, exactly `1372554837726243/1000000000000000000`.

This is 2.161253% above the pinned PR501/502 whole-owner result and 1.093987% above our previous asynchronous construction. It combines a new coordinated four-gauge target-level collapse, the PR495/501/502 body retiming, and offset6 asynchronous whole-owner hosting. All gains are recomputed from one actual paid program; no separately quoted exponent gains are added.

### New mechanism: release shared target levels together

Starting from PR484's gauge80-kernel42 word, helpers540,541,542,543 all move from rank4 entrance gauges to the existing rank2 frame `[408,102]`. The42 kernel pivots are unchanged. Reconstructing the entire frame system lowers targets81,82,84,87 from rank4 to rank2.

A single withdrawal leaves the shared target levels high. Four separately scored moves would predict only `-4 rank2 +4 rank4`. The actual joint change is `-16 rank2 +4 rank4 +4 rank6`: coordination releases costs that a marginal search misses. Four whole residuals grow from width5 to width7, so the changed inventory is repacked and charged in full.

The complete local inventory is18 width7,104 width8,438 width9. All72 calls use this same reconstructed provider. Eight replicas preserve their own controller order while calls follow `(7*stage+6*replica,stage,replica)`. All40320 helper uses have literal whole physical owners; no residual is split across families. Each invocation completes its whole cover sweep and normalization before another starts.

### Reproduction and checks

Additive folder: `research/coordinated-gauge-async/`.

```
python -B research/coordinated-gauge-async/verify.py --work /absolute/path/to/a-new-output-directory
```

Python3.11+, standard library only. No optimizer, network, C++ compiler or Lean installation is required. The output directory must be new and outside the package. Assertions must remain enabled.

The verifier reconstructs the public frame transfer and coordinated gauges, checks exact scalar columns in both orientations, Gaussian phases and paid wrappers, emits the physical asynchronous program, independently checks literal chronology/owners/spectators and the complete scalar/prefix invoice, and runs two rational moment engines plus six bootstrap steps and all47 strict outer inequalities. It rejects19 corrupt controller variants and4 outer controls, including the adjacent kappa grid point. The retained PR493 bit histogram is repriced; the unchanged bit operator is explicitly cited rather than needlessly re-run.

Generated text is forced to UTF-8/LF in a process-scoped launcher to avoid Windows/Linux adapter-hash mismatches. Immutable sources have a manifest and `.gitattributes`. Detailed receipts and the scope of local testing are included; this does not claim a CI run on an untested platform.

Our previous complete-invocation asynchronous construction supplies the scheduling method. OpenAI math's WordScheduling/CommonBases and the tensor-isomorphism intertwiner viewpoint informed the research; they are not represented as newly kernel-checked proofs of this package. Source revisions, file hashes, original notices and precise roles are included.

### Research preserved for future work

The package explains the nonlinear shared-target mechanism and retains concise evidence for382 single-gauge subframes,20 coordinated choices, six further combinations, retimed response-matroid variants, asynchronous inventory portfolios, and a clean-row alias screen. It also gives a sufficient pending-factor transport identity `Q_y A=A Q_x` and a safe deferred-terminal-suffix construction. Those additional routes produced no further priced gain here and are not counted in the exponent. Negative screens are bounded experiments, not global impossibility claims.

### Scope

This is a conditional finite whole-owner construction under the inherited all-size compiler, mutable-basis/common-label, normalized Lemma A realization, restored-row, precision/tape and analytic-transfer contracts. These remain explicit conditions; finite replay does not prove them. No unconditional integer-multiplication theorem or fresh Lean certification is claimed.

The snapshot is frozen through #504. #503's bit-only draft and #504's alternate read-then-climb route were read but are not numerical ingredients. #499's larger0.001452948511251494 claim inherits the disputed #494 split-residual interface; this submission neither adopts that interface nor claims to exceed that numerical headline.
